I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It has no lodash import and no hand-written replacements for the utilities. Type checking reports no errors for `out/module.ts`.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 242 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of that being my own code. I couldn't get the original's size to compare. `src/module.ts` can't be bundled here because lodash isn't installed, and `tsc` reports "Cannot find module" errors for it. I also didn't run the migrated functions against the original, so the equal-results check is untested. Below is the reasoning for each swap.

| lodash | es-toolkit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mapValues(scores, fn)` | `mapValues` | Same behaviour for plain objects with integer values. |
| `keyBy(rows, 'name')` | `keyBy(rows, (row) => row.name)` | es-toolkit's `keyBy` takes a function, not a property name. The one-line arrow is the only adapter. |
| `sortedUniq(values)` | `uniq(values)` | es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`. On sorted integer input, `uniq` gives the same result. |

`es-toolkit` (strict) was enough for all three, so `es-toolkit/compat` isn't used.
